title: TBX11K composition and partition sums
detail: partitions sum to 11190 (analysed 11190); positives 1190=924+212+54; 11190+10=11200

title: Table 1 row and total arithmetic
detail: all rows' pos+neg=images and prevalence reproduce; totals 16990/3928/13062 (23.12 %)

title: Internal test-set size: Table 1 vs Section 3.1 / Table 4
detail: Table 1: N=2238 (238 positive / 2000 negative). Section 3.1 and Table 4: N=2221 (404 / 1817). The results tables were evidently computed on a different test set than the revised dataset table describes.

title: Training-set size: Table 1 vs Section 3.2
detail: Table 1: 6714; Section 3.2: 6662.

title: Class-imbalance sampling weight is stale
detail: Reported 4.50 = 9085/2019 = 4.4998 (the earlier cohort). For the revised training split 6000/714 = 8.403. Which value was used in the reported experiments is unrecorded.

title: Table 4 MCC recomputed from Se, Sp and class counts
detail: max |MCC_reported - MCC_recomputed| = 0.0004 using N=2221 (404/1817); 0.0783 using Table 1's N=2238 (238/2000).

title: Which test-set size Table 4's exact binomial CIs correspond to
detail: max deviation (percentage points) of reported Clopper-Pearson bounds from recomputed ones: 0.62 with 404/1817 positives/negatives vs 1.94 with Table 1's 238/2000. The smaller value identifies the test set the intervals were computed on.

title: Table 4 AUC interval width vs the Hanley-McNeil approximation
detail: reported half-width / (1.96 x HM standard error) ranges 0.63-0.75 (mean 0.69). DeLong and Hanley-McNeil usually agree within ~10-15 %; values far below 1 suggest the intervals are narrower than the stated test-set size supports. Needs the prediction file to settle.

title: Ordering of the ten models is identical on AUC, sensitivity, specificity and MCC
detail: All four metrics are strictly increasing down the same ten-row ordering. A reviewer may ask whether each row is an independently trained model evaluated on the same cases.

title: Table 5 (padchest): ordering and interval width
detail: AUC/Se/Sp strictly increasing over 7 rows: True; AUC half-width / HM expectation 0.73-0.88.

title: Table 5 (tbportals): ordering and interval width
detail: AUC/Se/Sp strictly increasing over 7 rows: True; AUC half-width / HM expectation 1.18-1.31.

title: Table 6 delta-AUC arithmetic
detail: every delta equals mean - 0.971 to within rounding

title: Table 6 interval = mean +/- t(0.975, 4) x SD / sqrt(5)
detail: max deviation of the upper bound from the formula: 0.0000 (SD is rounded to 3 dp).

title: Same model, different AUC across Tables 4 and 6
detail: ResNet-50: Table 4 AUC 0.876 vs Table 6 A1 0.862 (same test set, same model). BioViL-T+LoRA: Table 4 0.961 vs Table 6 A3 (A2 with LoRA r16 a32) 0.913. Either the configurations differ in an undocumented way or the numbers come from different runs.

title: 'Without PRM' equals 'BioViL-T + LoRA'
detail: Table 6 A6c (DDFM + AGRN, no PRM) AUC 0.961 equals the plain BioViL-T+LoRA baseline 0.961 (and Table 8 repeats all five per-seed values). A model with two extra modules scoring exactly the baseline is possible but needs the run logs.

title: Relative-cost percentages in Section 3.5
detail: recomputed +21.6 % params, +24.9 % FLOPs, +77.7 % latency

title: Reported ViT-B/16 cost at 512x512 vs an analytic count
detail: Analytic multiply-accumulates for a 12-layer ViT-B/16 on 1,025 tokens: 107.0 G MACs (= 214.1 GFLOPs at 2 FLOPs per MAC). The manuscript reports 91.5 G 'FLOPs' (obtained by scaling the 224-px figure). The quantity measured is undefined; scripts/benchmark_efficiency.py states its convention and measures it.

title: Supplementary Table 1 parameter totals
detail: component rows sum to 18,321,675 trainable (18.3 M) and 104,634,123 in total (104.6 M).

title: Supplementary Table 1 lists modules absent from the main text
detail: It includes CrossScaleAttention (786,432 params) and per-band Linear(256->768) frequency projections (591,360), neither described in Section 2.4 / Figures 2-3, and shows the DDFM cross-attention input as (B,1025,768) whereas the text feeds a single 768-d vector. The 18.3 M figure depends on those modules.

title: Table 8 summaries follow from the printed per-seed values
detail: max |mean diff| 0.00000, |SD diff| 0.00002, |upper CI diff| 0.00004

title: Table 8 per-seed deviations follow a single template
detail: seed 42 equals the five-seed mean to 3 dp in all 8 rows: True. Deviations of seeds 0,1,2,3 from seed 42 are, in every row, a scalar multiple of one pattern (-0.0051, -0.0025, +0.0025, +0.0051); cosine similarity with MARS-TB's pattern: min 0.999899; scale factors MARS-TB:1.00, BioViL-T + LoRA:1.00, TBNet:1.24, MARS-TB without DDFM:1.24, MARS-TB without AGRN:1.00, MARS-TB without PRM:1.00, MT-EDL replaced with cross-entropy:1.00, LoRA replaced with full fine-tuning:1.50. Independent training runs do not normally produce deviations that are exactly proportional across eight models. These values should not be cited as measured results without the underlying run logs.

title: Table 8: exact constant offset and exact duplicate rows
detail: 'BioViL-T + LoRA' = 'MARS-TB' - 0.0000 spread around 0.0100 (constant offset: True); 'without PRM' is identical to 'BioViL-T + LoRA' in all five seeds: True.

title: Supplementary Tables S3-S5 arithmetic
detail: patient and 'additional radiograph' counts add up. Internal consistency does not show that the counts were observed: the manuscript's own text says patient counts for these cohorts were 'not established' (Section 2.1) while S3 reports 2,850 and 1,950 unique patients.

title: Supplementary Table S6: records satisfy the identities exactly and U sits on a 0.02 grid
detail: max identity error 0.0000. All 10 uncertainty values are exact multiples of 0.02 (0.08, 0.10, 0.06, 0.16, 0.12, 0.08, 0.10, 0.12, 0.16, 0.20), the signature expected if the Dirichlet parameters were back-computed from rounded (p, U), not read from raw model outputs. Raw model outputs are not normally this regular.

title: Holm family in Supplementary Table S8
detail: adjusting raw p = (0.003, 0.0005, 0.0005) over a family of 3 gives [0.003, 0.0015, 0.0015]; reported '0.003' and '<0.003' are consistent. (A p-value of exactly '<0.001' cannot be Holm-adjusted precisely.)

title: BioViL-T is not a ViT-B/16 (checked against the official model card, 2026-11-12)
detail: Manuscript Section 2.4.1: 'a ViT-B/16-based radiology image-text model ... 12 layers, 768, ~86 M'. Microsoft's model card (huggingface.co/microsoft/BiomedVLP-BioViL-T) describes 'a hybrid image encoder composed of a Vision Transformer and ResNet-50, where the latter is used as backbone network ... The transformer ... aggregate[s] and compare[s] image features extracted across the temporal dimension'. The official checkpoint cannot supply the 12-layer ViT-B/16 layers 4/8/12 the method needs.

title: Category-specific allocations cited to a table that is not that table
detail: Section 2.1 says 'Category-specific allocations are provided in Supplementary Table S1'; the supplementary file's Table 1 is the architecture parameter table. The per-category allocation is therefore not available.

title: 'Zero TBX11K patient overlap' cannot be established from TBX11K metadata
detail: Section 3.2 / Table 5 caption assert zero patient overlap between TBX11K and the external cohorts; Section 2.1 states patient identifiers and cross-dataset overlap were not established, and TBX11K documents no patient identifiers.

title: Image tensors: single channel (Fig. 1, Eq. 1) vs three channels (Table 2, Supp. Table 1)
detail: Figure 1 and Eq. 1 use (B,1,512,512); preprocessing replicates to three channels and Supplementary Table 1 has Conv2d(3,768,...). This repository uses 3-channel input and derives the single-channel DDFM input as the channel mean.
